current_state_challenges.challenge: 127 BRE rules require a full engineering deployment cycle for any change — business teams cannot modify product validation logic without engaging engineering, creating bottlenecks for new offer launches
Synchronous CSV processing causes CPU/heap overflows at scale — large validation batches (>10k rows) are unstable, forcing manual interventions and eroding operational trust in the pipeline
Silent failure modes — zombie transactions and untracked batch errors mean validation failures go undetected, creating data quality risk in the product-to-money chain
Speed-to-market pressure from Vivo and TIM — Claro's ability to launch new offers, bundles, and pricing tiers is bottlenecked by catalog rule governance
ANATEL Res. 680/2020 and LGPD require rule lineage, audit trails, and data classification controls — the legacy BRE provides none of these natively

business_impacts.impact: Engineering teams spend significant cycles on BRE maintenance and emergency patches rather than innovation
Unstable large-volume batch processing creates operational unreliability in the product validation pipeline
Undetected failures create data quality risk with downstream commercial and provisioning systems
Slow rule change cycle limits agility to respond to competitive offers or regulatory changes

industry_context.summary: Brazilian telecom is a three-player oligopoly (Claro, Vivo, TIM) under sustained competitive pressure on 5G, fiber, and digital offers. TM Forum standards and LGPD/ANATEL regulations are forcing carriers to modernize BSS/catalog stacks. Legacy BRE systems are an acknowledged industry liability — TM Forum case studies cite 3–6 month offer validation cycles on monolithic rule engines.
trends: Composable BSS/catalog architectures replacing monolithic BRE engines (TM Forum 2024)
LLM-native rule authoring and offer validation agents adopted by Tier-1 carriers (Telefónica, Vodafone, Orange)
Agentic automation in telco back-office reducing catalog rule authoring time by 50–70% vs. manual engineering
Real-time product catalog validation becoming table stakes for 5G bundle and convergent offer launches
regulatory_factors: LGPD (Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados) — requires consent/audit trails on all customer data processing; confirmed applicable to this engagement
ANATEL Res. 680/2020 — mandates real-time offer transparency and pricing justification; requires rule lineage in product catalog
competitive_pressures: Vivo (Telefónica) and TIM competing on 5G coverage and convergent bundle agility
Carriers differentiating on speed-to-market for new offers — target <30 days from product idea to offer; legacy BRE precludes this
ARPU pressure in Brazil driving cost-to-serve reduction via operational automation

value_drivers.driver: Self-service rule authoring via Agentforce PLM Admin
value_drivers.description: Business analysts author catalog rules in pt-BR natural language; Einstein LLM compiles to AST JSON; zero engineering deployment required. Rule change cycle reduces from weeks to minutes.
Async-first Queueable chain with byte-offset cursor eliminates CPU/heap overflows at scale. DLQ-first architecture ensures 100% failure capture — zero silent errors.
AST Walker replaces unpredictable BRE runtime with deterministic, in-memory evaluation at <50ms/record — predictable SLA, auditable logic.
Agentforce PLM Ops auto-generates HTML diagnostic reports per validation batch — reduces analyst investigation time from hours to seconds.
Immutable rule specs (Spec_Key + Source_Hash), compile snapshots, Platform Events, and Einstein Trust Layer provide full rule lineage and compliance audit trail.
PLM POC establishes the reference architecture for Agents 1 (KB), 3 (NBO), and 4 (Lead Qualification) — the full 4-agent Agentforce platform that governs the product-to-money chain.

transformation_strategy.vision_statement: Claro Brasil's product catalog becomes a strategic asset — governed by business teams in natural language, validated in milliseconds, and fully auditable for compliance. By replacing 127 brittle BRE rules with a self-authoring Agentforce engine, Claro breaks the dependency between catalog innovation and engineering cycles: a new product rule is written in Portuguese, compiled by AI, and live in production without a single deployment. The PLM POC is the first agent in a broader Agentforce platform that will govern the full product-to-money chain — from catalog validation to offer selection to lead qualification — positioning Claro as the carrier that moves fastest from product idea to customer offer.

principles.principle: AI for authoring, determinism for execution
principles.rationale: LLM compiles rules at authoring time; AST Walker evaluates them at runtime without LLM. No non-deterministic AI in the critical validation path — predictability and auditability are non-negotiable.
Every batch process runs asynchronously with full failure capture via Dead Letter Queues and Transaction Finalizers. Silent errors are architectural failures, not acceptable trade-offs.
Catalog rule authoring is democratized to business analysts via natural language. Schema validation, operator permission boundaries, and deployment controls remain engineering-owned.
All LLM traffic — rule compilation and diagnostic narrative — routes through Einstein Trust Layer. No raw Claro data reaches external models. LGPD compliance depends on this.
Every architectural decision in PLM is made as if it will be replicated for 3 additional agents. No one-offs; no shortcuts that create tech debt for the broader Agentforce platform.

Competitors Vivo and TIM are accelerating offer velocity on modern catalog stacks. The cost of inaction compounds each quarter.
